status: fixed an intermittent false-negative in OwnedProcess.terminate that left native PTY close cleanup pending; 30/30 terminal file runs clean afterwards

symptom.failure: captured.close(5) returned False in 0.1-0.2 s and backend.health() kept cleanup_pending=1
symptom.frequency: about 1/10 to 1/3 across repeated single-node runs under load; 9/10 on one full-file run

diagnosis.instrumented: temporary stderr diagnostics in TerminalProcess._close_actual and OwnedProcess.terminate (reverted before delivery)
diagnosis.observed: native_clean=True (worker reply skipped or false, host reclaim true) but helper_clean=False on the first attempt; terminate logged NoSuchProcess from psutil.Process(pid) while process.returncode was still None, then a second close attempt reclaimed cleanly
diagnosis.root_cause: the child can exit and be reaped before the asyncio transport publishes returncode; the identity lookup then raises psutil.NoSuchProcess and the broad except turned that into 'not reclaimed'. A SIGKILL racing with child exit (ESRCH) or a reused/unsignalable group (EPERM) had the same effect, and _group_quiet treated EPERM from kill(0) as 'not quiet'.

changes: psutil.NoSuchProcess during the identity check means there is no leader left to signal; wait() and the group scan still decide
os.killpg(SIGKILL) tolerates ESRCH/EPERM (exited leader or reused/unsignalable group) instead of failing the whole reclamation
_group_quiet falls through to the explicit member scan on EPERM from kill(0) and skips foreign processes that are not members of the owned group
fix.safety: reclamation is still only reported after wait() and a quiet owner-group scan; no unverifiable group is signalled or claimed clean

limits: The race window is inferred from instrumentation and eliminated in 30/30 runs; it is not proven impossible, only that the failure path now waits/scans instead of failing early.
Observed on macOS 27.2.1 arm64 only; Linux/Windows reclamation paths were not re-run natively.
The terminal close still depends on macOS session scanning; a long-lived foreign process with the same uid but an unreadable session could still return 'not quiet' by design.
Not whole-platform or whole-V2 acceptance; the 72-hour requirement remains open.
